reasons: No tests are visible for the layout or its navigation.
Phone users cannot reach the Family and Profile pages from the bottom menu.
The search input has no behaviour wired to it in this file.
The logout flow depends on the auth store, which is not shown here.

terms.meaning: A shared frame that wraps several pages so they look the same.
The vertical menu on the left side of the screen on large displays.
The web address path that decides which page is shown.
A shared place in the app that remembers who is signed in.
The step where the browser attaches the interactive parts to a page that was first drawn by the server.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and browser setup
sections.what: Loads the navigation helpers, icons, the auth store, styling helper, buttons and the shared pieces for profile switching and notifications. Marks the file as browser-only.
sections.why: The layout needs these pieces to draw the frame and react to the current address.
sections.watch_out: The file imports more pieces further down. This still works, but a new import added in the wrong place can be hard to find.

sections.name: navItems
sections.title: Menu items list
sections.what: Defines the seven menu entries, each with a name, a web address and an icon. Home, Timeline, Records, AI Chat, Reminders, Family and Profile.
sections.why: One list feeds both the sidebar and the phone menu, so the two stay in step.
sections.watch_out: Adding an item here changes both menus. The phone menu only shows the first five, so new items at the end will be hidden on phones.

sections.name: DashboardLayout (part 1)
sections.title: Layout start, sidebar and logout
sections.what: Reads the current address and the logout action. Draws the sidebar with the app name, the profile switcher, the menu list and a Log Out button. The sidebar only shows on large screens.
sections.why: The sidebar gives full navigation on desktops, and logout sits where users expect it.
sections.watch_out: The active item is found by an exact match on the address, so a sub-page like a deeper path will not highlight its parent menu item.

sections.name: DashboardLayout (part 2)
sections.title: Top bar with search and account
sections.what: Draws a sticky top bar with a search box, a notification centre and the account menu. The search box is labelled for screen readers and the bar stays visible while scrolling.
sections.why: Keeps common actions available on every page without scrolling back up.
sections.watch_out: The search box looks active but does nothing in this file, so users may type and see no results.

sections.name: DashboardLayout (part 3)
sections.title: Page content and phone menu
sections.what: Places the page content inside the main area with a skip-link for keyboard users, then draws a fixed bottom menu on phones with the first five items.
sections.why: The skip-link helps keyboard and screen reader users jump past the menus. The bottom menu gives phone users quick access to main pages.
sections.watch_out: Family and Profile are not shown in the phone menu. Any phone user has to rely on another path to reach them.

summary: The shared frame for all signed-in pages, with a left sidebar on large screens, a top bar with search and account controls, and a bottom menu on phones.
purpose: Gives every dashboard page the same navigation, logout button and page wrapper so users can move around the app.
why: Putting the navigation in one layout means each page does not need its own copy.
how: The layout reads the current web address to mark the active menu item. It draws the sidebar with a profile switcher, the main menu, and a logout button. The top bar holds a search box, notifications and the account menu. The page content is placed in the middle inside a transition wrapper. A short menu appears at the bottom on small screens.
inputs: The current web address, the page content passed in from each route, and the logout action in the auth store.
outputs: The drawn page frame, navigation links, and a return to the login page after logout.
risks: The bottom menu on phones only shows the first five items, so Family and Profile are not reachable there. The search box is drawn but does not run a search in this file. Logout clears the local login state and sends the user to login, but this file does not show any server-side sign-out.
debug: If a menu item is missing on phones, check the slice in the mobile navigation. If the active item is wrong, check that the link path exactly matches the current address. If logout seems to leave the user signed in, check the logout action in the auth store.
